title: Configure the service gateway in CC Switch
intro: The configuration itself is written by CC Switch; this tool never edits a config file for you. Review and edit the values below, test connectivity first, then either import them into CC Switch with one click or follow the manual steps.
codexClientNote: This configuration covers both Codex CLI and the Codex client / IDE extension — they share the same configuration under ~/.codex, so one setup serves both.

values.title: Values to enter
values.description: These are the values for CC Switch's “Add provider” form. Copy them as they are or press “Edit” to change them; after entering your API key, run “Test connectivity” once.
values.providerNameHint: Any name works; this one keeps things recognisable later.
values.baseUrlHint: Use it exactly as shown — do not add or remove a trailing slash or /v1.
values.protocolHint: The service gateway supports and recommends Responses. If the form has no such option, the current version already uses it by default.
values.protocolNoteClaude: Claude Code has no protocol setting — only the address, key and model are needed.
values.modelHintEmpty: There is no company-wide model name; enter the model you were assigned (or fetch the list from the gateway in the steps below).

test.description: Sends one minimal test request to the gateway using the address, model and key above.
test.needs: Enter the API address and API key to test (the model may stay empty).
test.notSent: No gateway request was sent this time: fix the problems flagged above and try again.

import.title: One-click import into CC Switch
import.description: Hands the values above straight to your local CC Switch (a recent version is required). CC Switch opens its own confirmation dialog and writes its own configuration — this tool still never touches any config file.
import.needsValues: Enter the provider name, API address and API key first (the model is optional).
import.editNote: Importing again creates a new provider instead of overwriting the old one; to change an existing provider, edit it inside CC Switch. The manual steps below remain available.
import.confirmBody: The link below will be opened so CC Switch can pre-fill the provider (the key is masked in this preview; the full key is sent). CC Switch will show its own confirmation dialog and only writes after you confirm there.
import.sent: Sent. Switch to the CC Switch window, confirm the import and “Use / Switch” the new provider so it becomes the current one, then come back here and continue.
import.failed: CC Switch could not be opened. Make sure a recent version of CC Switch is installed — or follow the manual steps below.

config.title: Codex config.toml template (recommended)
config.description: Paste this configuration into the “config.toml / configuration” field of the Codex provider in CC Switch (after the one-click import above, you can also edit that provider in CC Switch and replace its configuration with this). It routes through the service gateway while keeping most official features, and enables the priority tier, the large context window and auto-compaction for gpt-5.6-sol. The content is editable — for example, set a more radical model_auto_compact_token_limit or change any other default.
config.scopeHint: Choose what the 300000 auto-compaction threshold counts; when unsure, keep the recommended value.

body_after_prefix.label: body_after_prefix (recommended)
body_after_prefix.explanation: Counts only the conversation body after the cached prefix. More accurate with prompt caching and makes the most of the 372k context — the right choice in most cases.

total.label: total
total.explanation: Counts the whole request (prefix + body), so compaction triggers earlier. Pick this if you often hit context-exceeded errors or the gateway limits by total tokens.

config.keySubstitution: Copying replaces <API-KEY> with the real key entered above; the real key is never shown on screen.
config.keyMissing: No API key entered above yet: the copied content keeps the <API-KEY> placeholder — replace it yourself after pasting.
config.edited: Edited by hand: changing the values above or the accounting scope will not overwrite your changes; use “Restore generated template” when needed.

fastui.title: Codex client speed option without signing in (optional, Windows)
fastui.description: If you cannot sign in with a ChatGPT account, the Codex client hides its speed / tier option, even though the service gateway supports the priority tier. This tool from IT builds a separate copy of your installed Codex client with that one option unlocked. Your official installation is not modified and keeps working next to the copy, which gets its own shortcut and its own data directory.
fastui.caveat: This is an unofficial modification of the Codex client and is not supported by OpenAI. It is tested against {{build}} (toolkit {{version}}); on a newer Codex version the patcher stops instead of guessing, and you may need an updated toolkit from IT. Prefer the “Sign in with your ChatGPT account” step above whenever that is possible for you.
fastui.reversible: Everything happens inside your own user folder. “Undo the patch” restores the copy's original files, and deleting the folder removes it completely.
fastui.integrity: The bundled toolkit is checked against SHA-256 {{sha256}} before it runs.

confirm.install: Your official Codex client is copied to your user folder and the copy's interface files are patched. This takes a few minutes and needs a few gigabytes of free disk space. The installed Codex client is not touched.
confirm.verify: Re-checks the existing copy: that it still carries exactly the expected change, that its files are valid, and that it uses its own data directory.
confirm.restore: Puts the original files back into the copy, so it behaves like the official client again.

fastui.reinstallNote: A copy already exists. It is backed up and rebuilt from your current Codex client — close the copy first if it is running.
fastui.succeeded: Finished. Close and reopen the copy for the change to take effect.
fastui.failed: Did not finish. The output above shows why; you can retry or ask IT for an updated toolkit.

blocked.not_windows: This option is only available on Windows.
blocked.toolkit_missing: The toolkit is not bundled with this build, or its integrity check failed. Please ask IT.
blocked.codex_app_missing: The official Codex client was not found. Install it first, start it once, then come back.
blocked.not_installed: There is no patched copy yet — create one first.

models.fetch: Fetch model list from the gateway
models.hint: Uses the address and key from “Values to enter”.
models.needsKey: Enter the API address and API key under “Values to enter” first to fetch the model list.
models.empty: The gateway returned no models; enter the model name you were assigned.
models.listLabel: Models reported by the gateway (click to use)

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: Follow these in order inside CC Switch. Steps with an “I did this” button can be checked by the tool.

open_cc_switch.title: Open CC Switch
open_cc_switch.body: Find CC Switch in the Start menu / Launchpad and open it. If it is not installed yet, go back to the “Install” step first.

login_chatgpt.title: Sign in with your ChatGPT account (optional)
login_chatgpt.body: Once CC Switch is installed, it is worth signing in to Codex with your ChatGPT account first: open a terminal, run codex and pick “Sign in with ChatGPT”. Being signed in keeps the official login-gated features (such as the speed / tier option) available, which works best together with the config.toml template below. This step is optional — skipping it does not affect the rest of the setup.

select_tool_tab.title: Switch to the {{tool}} tab
select_tool_tab.body: CC Switch has Claude / Codex tabs at the top (or on the left). Pick “{{tool}}”. If you use both tools, configure each one separately.

add_provider.title: Click “Add provider”
add_provider.body: On the {{tool}} tab click “Add provider” (it may be labelled “New” or “+”). A form opens.

paste_base_url.title: Paste the API address
paste_base_url.body: Paste the address below into “API address / Base URL” exactly as shown. Do not add or remove a trailing slash or /v1; the connectivity test under “Values to enter” shows the address that will actually be used.

choose_protocol.title: Choose the protocol: {{protocol}}
choose_protocol.body: Under “Protocol / request format” choose “{{protocol}}”. It is the protocol the service gateway supports and recommends; if the option is missing, the default is already correct.

paste_api_key.title: Paste your API key
paste_api_key.body: Paste the key you were issued into “API key”. Make sure there is no space or line break at the beginning or end — that is the most common cause of authentication failures (401). Best run the connectivity test under “Values to enter” first; it checks the format along the way.

set_model.title: Enter the model
set_model.body: In “Model” enter: {{model_hint}}. This value can differ per person — use the one you were assigned, or fetch the list from the gateway below and pick one.

save_and_activate.title: Save and switch to this provider
save_and_activate.body: Click “Save”. A newly added provider is not active automatically: click “Use / Switch” in the list so it becomes the current provider (the card usually changes colour or shows a check mark).

close_terminals.title: Close every terminal window
close_terminals.body: The configuration does not take effect in terminals that are already open. Close all terminal windows, including the built-in terminals of VS Code, Cursor and similar editors (safest: quit the editor entirely).

verify.title: Verify
verify.body: Click “Next” below. The tool checks {{tool}} in a fresh terminal session and can optionally send one test request to the gateway.

key.privacy: The key stays in this page's memory only — used for the connectivity test, the model list and, after you confirm, the one-click import. It is never written to disk, logged or uploaded, and is cleared when you leave this page.
key.invalid: The key format has problems that need fixing:

issue.leading_or_trailing_whitespace: There is a space / tab at the beginning or end. Some whitespace was selected when copying — remove it and paste again.
issue.contains_whitespace: Contains a space in the middle. Keys have no spaces; the copy may have wrapped or picked up extra text.
issue.contains_newline: Contains a line break. Paste it as a single line (try pasting into a plain text editor first).
issue.non_ascii: Contains non-Latin or full-width characters. Switch to an English keyboard layout and paste again.
issue.unexpected_prefix: Does not start with the usual sk-. Key formats differ between gateways; ignore this if the key came from the gateway.
issue.too_short: Looks short. Make sure the whole key was copied.
issue.looks_like_placeholder: Looks like example placeholder text (e.g. <your-key>, sk-xxxx), not a real key.

rule.already_versioned: The address already ends in /v1 and is used as-is.
rule.appended_v1: Only a host was given, so /v1 is appended automatically.
rule.literal_hash: A trailing # means “use literally” — nothing is appended. Only use this when the gateway explicitly asks for it.
rule.custom_path: A custom path is kept as-is. Unless the gateway requires it, switch back to the service gateway address.
rule.invalid: This is not a valid address. Please check it and try again.

warning.not_https: The address is not https, so traffic would be unencrypted. Make sure this is what the gateway requires.
warning.trailing_slash_removed: The trailing slash is removed automatically.
warning.contains_whitespace: The address contains whitespace — remove it.
warning.contains_credentials: The address contains a username / password. Never put the key into the address.
warning.looks_like_chat_completions_endpoint: The address ends in /chat/completions, which is an endpoint path rather than a Base URL — remove that part.
warning.differs_from_company_gateway: This differs from the service gateway address. Unless there is a specific reason, use the service gateway address.

closeTerminals.title: After saving in CC Switch, close ALL terminal windows
closeTerminals.body: Terminals that are already open will not see the new configuration — including the built-in terminals of VS Code, Cursor and similar editors. Close them all before moving on to verification.

reminders.noWrite: This tool never edits ~/.codex, ~/.claude or CC Switch configuration files; the one-click import merely hands the values to CC Switch, which writes its own configuration after you confirm.
